newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF half year profits jump nearly 50 percent.
newsitem.headline: AGF half year profits jump nearly 50 percent.

text.p: Newly privatised French insurer AGF reported on Thursday a nearly 50 percent jump in half-year profit on Thursday, helped by a turnaround in non-life activities and a strong contribution from foreign operations.
Assurances Generales de France said consolidated net profit climbed to 723 million francs ($140.5 million) from 487 million on premium income which rose 5.4 percent to 33.8 billion.
"The improvement in results is gathering pace," France's second largest insurance group said, adding it had built up its position in core activities and disposed of unprofitable assets.

AGF, which took big provisions to cover its exposure to France's depressed property market in the run-up to its sell-off last May, said it was on target to achieve its aim of a 10 percent return on equity by end 1999, up from 6.3 percent.
But the results failed to impress investors. AGF shares closed down 3.50 francs or 2.46 percent at 138.50 francs with some analysts questioning the quality of the profits.

"The profit improvement has come from capital gains and reducing the debt burden and not from the insurance business which is their core business," said one analyst. But others disagreed, and said AGF was making good progress.
As part of a drive to dispose of unprofitable holdings, AGF said it sold 5.76 billion francs worth of real estate in France and Spain and invested the cash in higher-yielding securities.
It also sold 2.75 billion francs worth of stocks for a gain of 883 million francs, part of plans to sell five to seven billion francs of equity stakes over 24 months.

Losses of the group's holding firms were slashed to 37 million francs from 466 million, reflecting capital gains on sale of investments and reduced debt servicing costs as a result of lower interest rates.

Life insurance kicked in 131 million francs to earnings before exceptional items, down from 344 million. But that reflected the one-off impact of its successful Valorea contract sold by the French postal service on the 1995 figures.
Non-life insurance added 364 million francs to profits, up by nearly 12 percent, reflecting better underwriting profits.

Business was particularly strong outside France with AGF's Spanish unit swinging to a profit of 27 million from a loss of 53 million. The Canadian unit had half-year earnings of 17 million compared with a loss of five million. And the Belgian unit's profits soared to 225 million from 125 million.
Losses from banking activities grew to 346 million from a loss of 203 million but that reflected a 245 million franc addition to reserves to cover losses on future disposals.

Its property lending arm, Comptoir des Entrepreneurs, which hemorrhaged red ink in the past, slashed its loss to 32.5 million francs from 67 million. But the loss of Banque du Phenix rose to 51 million from a loss of 36 million a year earlier and AGF reiterated it wanted to dispose of it as soon as possible.
Property units had a loss of 67 million francs, up from a loss of seven million, reflecting higher provisions. ($1=5.145 French Franc)
